newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Egypt's Mubarak in Zimbabwe for G-15 summit.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak in Zimbabwe for G-15 summit.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak arrived in Harare amid tight security on Saturday to attend a Group of 15 (G-15) meeting on the trade concerns of developing countries.

Scores of heavily armed Zimbabwean soldiers milled around Harare airport, with some posted on rooftops, while dozens of Egyptian security men -- several of them with guns in full view -- patrolled the tarmac as Mubarak inspected a guard of honour.

There was a bit of heated debate between Egyptian officials and their local counterparts as Mubarak and Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe were led to a Zimbabwe Air Force helicopter which whisked them away, escorted by three other helicopters.

Zimbabwean officials said the visitors were miffed at the transport arrangements as they wanted their own convoy -- comprising four bullet-proof jeeps, an ambulance and a couple of Mercedes Benz car -- to take Mubarak into town.
The officials said the jeeps and ambulance were flown into Harare from Egypt on Friday night.
"They wanted to sideline us and take over all the arrangements concerning their president," one official who refused to be identified told Reuters.

Mubarak -- whose visit Egypt had not announced in advance apparently for security reasons -- has not travelled south of his country since Islamist militants tried to kill him in July 1995 as he arrived in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa for an Organisation of African Unity summit.

In Harare, he joined Malaysian Prime Minister Mathir Mohamad, India's H.D. Deve Gowda and Argentinian Vice President Carlos Ruckauf who arrived earlier on Saturday for the G-15 meeting starting on Sunday.
Organisers of the G-15 said on Friday eight heads of state and government had confirmed their attendance but they declined to name them, citing security reasons.

The leaders will map out strategies for promoting trade between them and for stimulating growth in the world's poorest regions. They will also look at ways of forging a common front among African, Asian and Latin American states to give them a stronger voice in a world moving towards free trade.
The G-15 comprises Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe.
